claims.claim_text: The indexed Sverre B. Rogne is the Norwegian merchant seaman later listed with Company C, 99th Infantry Battalion (Separate).
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The three records share the distinctive exact name; the Norwegian register also documents migration to the United States and wartime merchant service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an uncommon exact name, compatible Norwegian background, U.S. migration, merchant-seaman chronology, and matching Norwegian-American Army unit.
claims.temporal_assessment: Merchant-vessel work is documented through June 1942 and U.S. Army unit membership during 1941-1945; the exact OSS transfer date is not stated.
claims.match_notes: Rogne and Rockne are retained as documented variants. The personnel file remains the best route to exact transfer chronology.

claims.claim_text: Sverre B. Rogne's latest documented civilian work before his U.S. Army service was as a merchant seaman aboard M/S Pleasantville in 1942.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Norwegian register records Rogne's engagement aboard M/S Pleasantville from May 28 until the vessel was torpedoed in June 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the distinctive exact name and corroborating Norwegian-American military context.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded before the separately documented Army unit affiliation; not proven to be the immediate pre-OSS role.
claims.match_notes: The vessel is the documented workplace. The source does not identify a separate payroll employer or shipowner.

claims.claim_text: Sverre B. Rogne served with Company C, 99th Infantry Battalion (Separate).
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Denver Public Library's 10th Mountain Division index lists the exact name in Company C, 99th Infantry.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the uncommon exact name and compatible Norwegian wartime biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: The roster establishes service during the 1941-1945 database period but does not state that this assignment immediately preceded OSS.
claims.match_notes: Published as a military assignment, never as a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George F. Rohrlich is the economist documented at Brookings Institution and Sweet Briar College during 1942-1944.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Two contemporary scholarly records use the exact distinctive name and document a coherent Brookings-to-Sweet Briar professional chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name, the index's civilian WAE status, and mutually consistent contemporary academic sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Brookings is described as former in August 1942; Sweet Briar employment is documented in 1942 and May 1944. The OSS entry date is unknown.
claims.match_notes: The personnel file remains necessary to establish the immediate pre-OSS relationship and precise WAE chronology.

claims.claim_text: George F. Rohrlich was an instructor in Sweet Briar College's Division of Social Studies by August 1942 and remained affiliated in May 1944.
claims.evidence_excerpt: appointed instructor in the division of social studies at Sweet Briar College
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary professional notice reports the appointment; his 1944 journal article lists Sweet Briar College as his affiliation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact distinctive name and two mutually consistent contemporary publications.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented during 1942-1944, but neither source establishes that the job immediately preceded OSS service.
claims.match_notes: Published as other documented pre-OSS-era employment, not as the immediate predecessor.

claims.claim_text: George F. Rohrlich had a documented pre-Sweet Briar affiliation with the Brookings Institution.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Dr. George F. Rohrlich, formerly of the Brookings Institution
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The August 1942 professional notice describes Rohrlich as formerly of Brookings before announcing his Sweet Briar appointment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact distinctive name and internally explicit professional sequence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Definitely before the August 1942 Sweet Briar appointment; the source does not state the Brookings role, dates, or proximity to OSS.
claims.match_notes: Modeled as a professional affiliation rather than employment because the source only says 'formerly of.'
